title: Categorical structure of probability distributions under convolution

problemStatement.formal: (ProbMeasure, convolution, diracProb 0) forms a commutative monoid; CLT = convergence in this monoid
problemStatement.plain: Probability distributions on ℝ form a commutative monoid under convolution with Dirac delta as identity. The CLT says normalized convolution powers converge to the Gaussian fixed point.
whyMatters: Reveals algebraic structure underlying the CLT
Connects probability theory to category theory and abstract algebra
Cramér's theorem shows Gaussian is 'prime' in this monoid

proven: convPow_add: μ^{*(m+n)} = μ^{*m} * μ^{*n} (proved by induction)
convolution_dirac_left': derived from commutativity + right identity
clt_domain_of_attraction: CLT = membership in DOA of Gaussian
gaussian_in_own_domain: Gaussian is in its own DOA
knownResults.goal: Formalize the commutative monoid structure and CLT as convergence in this structure

currentState.focus: Complete formalization of convolution monoid and CLT categorical interpretation

knowledge.progressSummary: Created CentralLimitTheoremOQ03.lean (Docker-verified, 1 sorry). Formalizes: (1) ProbMeasure type wrapping Mathlib measures, (2) convolution as axiomatized binary operation with monoid axioms, (3) convolution powers with proved distribution law, (4) characteristic function homomorphism property, (5) domain of attraction formalization with CLT as DOA membership, (6) Gaussian stability and Cramér's indecomposability theorem, (7) full monoid summary theorem.
insights: The CLT has a clean categorical interpretation: Gaussian is the attractor in the convolution monoid under normalization
Cramér's theorem gives algebraic 'primality' of the Gaussian - it cannot be decomposed as a non-trivial convolution
Domain of attraction is closed under convolution (with variance condition)
Characteristic functions provide a homomorphism from (ProbMeasure, conv) to (ℂ^ℝ, ·)
convPow_add distributes nicely via induction + associativity
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has MeasureTheory.Measure.conv but not a ProbMeasure-level convolution
Lévy continuity theorem (charFun convergence ↔ distribution convergence) not in Mathlib

approaches.name: Axiomatized convolution monoid
approaches.description: Axiomatize convolution at the ProbMeasure level and prove monoid properties, then state CLT as convergence in this structure.
